subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A lift accelerates upward at 2 m/s^2 carrying a 50 kg person (g = 9.8). The normal reaction is:
A 5 kg mass has weight (g = 9.8) of:
questions.explain: Weight = mg = 5 x 9.8 = 49 N.

questions.q: On a slope at angle theta, the component of weight perpendicular to the slope is:
questions.explain: The perpendicular component, balancing the normal reaction, is W cos(theta).

questions.q: The maximum (limiting) friction force is given by:
questions.explain: At the point of slipping, friction equals mu times the normal reaction.

questions.q: For the 3 kg and 5 kg pulley system (a = 2.45, g = 9.8), the string tension is:
A 3 kg mass on a rough 30 degree slope (mu = 0.2, g = 9.8) has friction at limiting equilibrium of about:
A 2 kg block on a rough table (mu = 0.4, g = 9.8) has limiting friction of:
A 10 kg block is pulled by a 30 N horizontal force against 10 N friction. Its acceleration is:
Newton's third law says forces between two bodies are:
options: equal and in the same direction
questions.explain: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

questions.q: Two connected blocks (4 kg and 6 kg) on a smooth table are pulled by 20 N. Their acceleration is:
questions.explain: Total mass 10 kg: a = 20/10 = 2 m/s^2.

questions.q: A resultant force of 12 N acts on a 4 kg mass. Its acceleration is:
questions.explain: F = ma gives a = 12/4 = 3 m/s^2.

questions.q: Three forces keep a particle in equilibrium. They must:
questions.explain: For equilibrium under three forces, they form a closed vector triangle.

questions.q: A 4 kg block on a rough horizontal surface (mu = 0.25, g = 9.8) needs what minimum force to start moving?
questions.explain: Limiting friction = mu mg = 0.25 x 4 x 9.8 = 9.8 N.

questions.q: The friction model F <= mu R means friction:
questions.explain: Friction can be anything up to its maximum value mu R.

questions.q: A 2 kg object hangs in equilibrium from a string (g = 9.8). The tension is:
questions.explain: In equilibrium T = mg = 2 x 9.8 = 19.6 N.

questions.q: A car (mass 1000 kg) accelerates at 1.5 m/s^2. The driving force (no resistance) is:
Forces 8 N east and 5 N west act on a particle. The resultant is:
questions.explain: 8 - 5 = 3 N in the direction of the larger force, east.

questions.q: A lift descends with acceleration 2 m/s^2 carrying 60 kg (g = 9.8). The reaction force is:
A particle on a slope inclined at 30 degrees has weight W. The component along the slope is:
questions.explain: The component of weight down the slope is W sin(theta).

questions.q: A particle is in equilibrium when the resultant force is:
questions.explain: Equilibrium means the vector sum of forces is zero.

questions.q: Two masses 3 kg and 5 kg hang over a smooth pulley. The acceleration (g = 9.8) is:
A force of 10 N at 60 degrees above horizontal has a horizontal component of:
questions.explain: Horizontal component = 10 cos 60 = 10 x 0.5 = 5 N.

questions.q: For a body moving at constant velocity, the resultant force is:
questions.explain: Constant velocity means no acceleration, so resultant force is zero.

questions.q: A box of weight 60 N rests on a horizontal floor. The normal reaction is:
questions.explain: On level ground with no other vertical force, R = weight = 60 N.

questions.q: A block slides down a smooth 30 degree incline. Its acceleration (g = 9.8) is:
A 1200 kg car experiences 800 N resistance while driving force is 2000 N. Acceleration is:
A particle rests in limiting equilibrium on a rough slope. Friction acts:
questions.explain: Friction opposes the tendency to slide, acting up the slope.

questions.q: In that 4 kg + 6 kg system (a = 2), the tension in the string pulling the 4 kg block is:
questions.explain: For the 4 kg block: T = ma = 4 x 2 = 8 N.

questions.q: Newton's first law states a body continues at rest or constant velocity unless:
questions.explain: A change in motion requires a non-zero resultant force.

questions.q: A particle is held by two strings at 90 degrees to each other, tensions 3 N and 4 N. The weight supported is:
questions.explain: Resultant of perpendicular tensions = sqrt(3^2+4^2) = 5 N, balancing weight.
